content.title: Warriors assistants reportedly don't expect Steve Kerr to return next season
content.text: Uncertainty has been a common theme hovering over the Warriors this season, and that only amplified after Jimmy Butler's season-ending ACL injury this week. Now, longtime Warriors coach Steve Kerr's future with the organization appears to be heading toward an amicable split more than ever before. With Kerr in the final year of his current contract, several assistant coaches "have been operating under the premise" that Kerr will not return to Golden State next season, The Ringer's Logan Murdock reported in a column published Wednesday, citing team sources. These reported coaches have begun to survey the league to ensure they have jobs next season, Murdock added. Two seasons ago, assistant coach Kenny Atkinson departed the Warriors to become the head coach of the Cleveland Cavaliers. In the middle of this season, assistant Chris DeMarco left his duties in Golden State to venture into the WNBA as the head coach of the New York Liberty. Kerr and the Warriors' decision makers have been on the same page about the coach's future with the organization. At the end of last season, Kerr labeled it as "year-to-year." Dunleavy ensured that Kerr will have the job as long as he wants to. Nothing changed a few months later as Kerr and Dunleavy spoke to reporters again before the start of the 2025-26 season. Dunleavy maintained his stance that Kerr can stay as long as he wants, adding that he wants to give him "the grace of the season to go through it" and feel where he's at mentally and physically. Kerr hasn't publicly changed his tone on where things stand, but given how the season has gone in addition to Butler's injury, he could have a different outlook. Many, including both Kerr and Steph Curry, had hoped they would end their Warriors careers at the same time while acknowledging that the contract timelines didn't align. Now, it's anyone's guess.
